info.desc: Neon Bible is the second album by Canadian indie rock band Arcade Fire, released in March 2007 on Merge Records. Originally announced on December 16, 2006 through the band's website, the majority of the album was recorded in a church that the band bought and renovated. Neon Bible became Arcade Fire's highest charting album at the time, debuting on the Billboard 200 at number two, selling 92,000 copies in its first week and more than 400,000 to date. Being released within a month of similarly successful releases by The Shins (Wincing the Night Away) and Modest Mouse (We Were Dead .

podcast.body: Recorded mostly in the band's self-purchased church headquarters in Farnham, Quebec, with some sessions in New York, this album was released on March 7, 2007. It explored themes of dissonance and dread, influenced by Win Butler's outsider perspective on the US while living in Canada. *Neon Bible* debuted at No. 1 in Canada and Ireland, No. 2 in the US and UK, No. 7 in Australia, and No. 9 in France. It garnered "unanimously ecstatic" reviews (except for Rolling Stone, which felt "a little cold"), became Merge Records' best-selling album, was a finalist for the 2007 Polaris Music Prize, received a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Album (losing to The White Stripes' *Icky Thump*), and won a Juno in the same category. "They called this album Neon Bible."

podcast.body: This album was a finalist for the 2007 Polaris Music Prize and received a nomination for Best Alternative Album at the Grammys, where it lost to "Icky Thump" by The White Stripes. It did, however, win a Juno in the same Best Alternative Album category. This marked the second consecutive album from the independent Canadian band to achieve significant global recognition. It is estimated to have sold around one million copies worldwide. "Neon Bible may have sold a million copies worldwide."
